summary: Flaky timing assertions: the 'timing guard' test asserts wall-clock bounds (full read of a 30 MB journal < 15 s, incremental read < max(250 ms, full/4)) measured with performance.now(). On a loaded shared CI runner (Windows, ARM, parallel shards) a GC pause or disk stall during the second read can exceed 250 ms even when the reader is correctly incremental, so the test can go red without a code regression.
fix: Assert incrementality structurally instead of by time: expose or observe the bytes read (e.g. state offset advanced only by the appended line length, or spy on fs.readSync byte counts) and drop the ms thresholds, or keep timing only as a soft log.

summary: The Claude child launch test waits for the backgrounded fake claude to write its args file with a fixed 50 x 100 ms poll (5 s ceiling). On a slow runner the detached child may not have run yet, and the following readFileSync throws ENOENT, failing the test on scheduling rather than on launch behavior.
fix: Have the fake binary signal completion deterministically (e.g. wait on a FIFO or poll with a generous deadline tied to the test timeout) and fail with a clear message if the args file never appears.

summary: nonceSessions binds a session by reading every Claude Code journal under every project directory fully into memory as a UTF-8 string (readFileSync per file) just to find the nonce. fix: Limit the scan to recently modified journals (sort by mtime, check the newest N or those touched in the last few minutes) and search each one in fixed-size chunks or just its tail, since the nonce was echoed in the current session; stop early once two matches already mean refusal.

summary: Under delegation, the parent's close marks the child's reviews as unreserved. While the child runs, verify-handoff points the shared per-branch marker at the child ledger, so the child's Step 9 and 11 review-log starts consume reservations in the child ledger. At parent close, unreservedDispatches reads the shared review log and matches rows only against the parent's own reservations, so every child review row has no match. close then prints BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED and stops status=incomplete for the owner to accept. Steps 7 and 12 delegate whenever the per-call charge is unknown, which is always true on the estimate meter and on Capy without --prior-reading, so most delegated capped runs end this way. The full-chain test closes without child review rows, so nothing covers it.
fix: In unreservedDispatches, also match rows against reconciled children's ledgers, or skip rows whose start falls inside a reconciled handoff window. Add a chain test where the child logs a review.

summary: Under a cap, Step 9's design-review-lite start gets refused. The template still says to run `gstack-review-log --start design-review-lite` with no `--reservation`. While the cap marker exists, admitReviewStart refuses any start without an unspent dispatch reservation (exit 1, BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED). The batch reservation for Step 9 is one-shot and gets spent on `--start review`. So any capped /ship on a frontend diff fails at design review, and no prose tells the agent to reserve for it.
fix: Add the reservation instruction to the design-review-lite start, or fold it into the Step 9 batch with its own reservation, and add a section test for it.

summary: A stopped or abandoned capped run blocks later reviews on its branch, standalone /review included. On budget_exhausted, context_threshold or budget_check_skipped, the run keeps its per-branch marker and l.stopped stays set. Every later `gstack-review-log --start` on that branch then fails with BUDGET_CAP_REACHED, and the message gives no fix. A failed reservation check fails the same way. This lasts until someone runs gstack-ship-budget resume or close.
fix: Have the stop path unlink or park the marker, or scope admission to /ship starts (for example, with an env flag set by /ship). Give the refusal a fix line that names resume or close.

label: FIXABLE
summary: A child's own reviews get flagged as unreserved when the parent closes, so every capped run that delegates Steps 7-11.5 (or 12-22) ends status=incomplete. lib/ship-budget.ts unreservedDispatches() matches review-log rows against l.reservations, which holds the parent's reservations only. A child run (cmdVerifyHandoff) writes to the same review_log (parent.review_log) but keeps its reservations in its own child ledger, and cmdReconcile never merges them back. Step 9 "review" and Step 11 "adversarial-review" rows from the child start after the parent's created_at and have no parent reservation within 5 s. Parent `close` therefore prints BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED for each one, sets stopped, and exits 3. The "full chain" test runs close without any child review-log dispatch, so this path is untested. Fix: at reconcile, record the child run id and include the child ledger's consumed reservations in the audit, or exclude rows inside reconciled handoff windows.

label: FIXABLE
summary: Consumed dispatch reservations never expire, so one missed --finish adds a permanent 7.43M phantom charge and causes false BUDGET_CAP_REACHED stops. tally() counts 'consumed' reservations in `reserved` while the Capy or Claude meter also counts the real spend in `used`, so the cost is counted twice until settle. cmdCheck auto-settles open *step* reservations but never dispatch ones. Only `gstack-review-log --finish <same token>` or a manual `settle` clears them. Any dispatch that errors, gets logged without --finish, or finishes while the marker points at another ledger (settleReviewFinish silently returns undefined; the review-log wrapper swallows failures with `|| true`) stays consumed for the rest of the run. With per_dispatch=7,430,000, one leaked two-role batch (14.86M) uses up most of a 25M cap. close only reports `open_dispatches=N`. Fix: settle consumed dispatch reservations once the run checks past the dispatch's step, or at least at the next `check`, as steps already are.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The review-log gate marker is keyed by branch, not by run, so a capped run can gate or un-gate unrelated reviews. reviewPaths() puts the marker at `<state>/projects/<slug>/<BRANCH>-ship-budget.json`. bin/gstack-slug turns every detached HEAD into BRANCH=HEAD, so every detached worktree of the repo shares one marker. One capped /ship then makes `gstack-review-log --start` in every other detached checkout demand that run's reservations (BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED), or refuse outright once it stops (BUDGET_CAP_REACHED). The marker also goes stale and gets stolen: (a) cmdStart's unmetered no-cap path returns before pointMarker, so a stopped or abandoned capped run keeps blocking plain `/review` on that branch until someone runs close or resume. The refusal text never names that recovery. (b) A second capped start overwrites the first run's marker, so the first run's reservation ids become "not in run". (c) cmdClose unlinks the marker without checking that it points at itself, which silently drops the gate for a concurrent run. (d) A corrupt marker JSON or a missing ledger makes activeLedger throw, which fails every review start on the branch. Fix: bind the gate to the run (pass the run id through the environment to review-log, or keep a per-run marker set), unlink only a marker that points at this run, and treat an unreadable marker or a dead ledger as no cap, with a warning.

label: FIXABLE
summary: A Drive checkpoint write failure leaves orphan reservations and a nonstandard exit code. writeLedger() writes the ledger, then the record block, then mirrorRun() into Drive, all inside withFileLock. The checkpoint is on by default whenever GSTACK_CAPY=1 and exactly one project-user drive exists. If the Drive write throws (drive cap, mount unavailable, slow I/O past the 10 s lock timeout that other contenders hit), the local ledger already holds the new reservation. The bin then rethrows the non-BudgetError: stack trace, exit 1, and no RESERVATION line printed. Each retry by the agent adds another orphan open or consumed reservation, so a transient Drive fault becomes a budget stop. In admitReviewStart, capture() has already run (the start token is written) when this happens. Fix: make mirrorRun best-effort, catching the error and printing a warning, and run it after the lock is released.

label: FIXABLE
summary: A delegated child stops at its own segment boundary whenever the per-call charge is unknown. decide(): `wants = boundary && (call === null || call >= 150k)`, and `role === 'child'` turns wants into STOP context_threshold. On Capy, call is null unless the agent passes --prior-reading, which the section presents as optional. A start-delegated child (Steps 1-22) therefore always stops at `--next 7` and writes status=incomplete. The parent reconciles with exit 3 and is told to "regenerate the handoff", which produces the same child and the same stop: an endless loop that burns tokens. Fix: in a child, only a measured call >= threshold should stop; or skip the 7 and 12 boundaries inside a 1-22 child segment.

label: FIXABLE
summary: verify-handoff never claims the handoff, so duplicate children each get the full sub-cap. cmdVerifyHandoff reads the parent ledger without the lock and without mutating it. Two launches of the same brief (a retried `launch`, or a Capy subagent restarted) both pass verification, both mint child runs with cap=sub_cap, and both believe they are "the only writer" of the record. The parent reserved one sub-cap, so real spend can reach twice that. pointMarker also flips the marker to whichever child verified last, which makes the other child's dispatches refuse. Fix: in verify-handoff, under mutateLedger on the parent, set handoff.verified_by=<child run> and refuse a second claim.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The record's gstack-budget block breaks on paths that contain spaces. recordBlock() writes `ledger=${l.file}` unquoted, and parseRecordBlock() splits on /\s+/. A state root such as "C:<home>/.gstack", a macOS "Application Support" path, or a `--ledger` path with a space truncates the ledger path. Every `--record` command (check, resume, start re-attach, rebuild) then fails with BUDGET_LEDGER_INVALID "missing". Fix: JSON-encode the block body.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: Cap raises are self-attested, and rebuild-from-record skips the journal entirely. `resume --token-cap <n|none> --approved-by X --words Y` accepts any strings from the capped agent itself. `none` deletes the marker and removes all gating. Separately, `--rebuild-from-record` trusts the cap= / used= / role= fields in the record, a markdown file the agent edits throughout the run, and runs whenever readLedger fails. Deleting or corrupting the ledger and editing the block yields any cap with an empty cap_raises journal. A rebuilt child also loses `parent`, so its `return` refuses ("not a child run") and its stop writes no return file. Decide whether the owner approval must be verifiable (gstack-approvals record or a signed token), or explicitly accept that the cap is advisory against the agent.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: A premature reconcile orphans a child that is still running. cmdReconcile has no liveness check (launch never stores the pid in the ledger). Reconciling before the return file exists marks the handoff interrupted, settles the child reservation, and points the marker back at the parent. The detached child keeps spending: its dispatches now fail as "not in run", and on meter=estimate its spend goes unrecorded. Its later return is ignored as already reconciled. Consider recording the pid or session id and refusing to reconcile a child that is alive without --force.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: The calibration makes the documented flagship cap almost unreachable. The constants (per_call 750k, per_dispatch 7.43M, stop_overhead 2.48M, tail 2M) give Step 7 a projection of 12x750k + 7.43M = 16.43M, and a two-role Step 9 batch 14.86M, each plus 4.48M held back. Under `--token-cap 25M`, the docs' own example, Step 7 is admitted only if used <= ~4.1M, and a full-depth 4-role batch (29.7M) can never be admitted. Each projection prices every call at 1.5x the worst late-run call. Expect most 25M runs to stop at Step 7 or 9 with nothing shipped. This needs a product call on the fit before the docs promote 25M.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The close audit matches rows by a ±5 s timestamp window and lets one reservation cover several starts. unreservedDispatches() accepts any reservation whose started_at falls within 5 s of a row's started_at and never consumes the match, so an unreserved start beside a reserved one passes the audit. The `reservedStarts.has(startFile.token)` test is tautological, since startFile was selected for having started_at and token. Match on the start token instead.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: The brief controls file writes and launch behavior. verify-handoff writes `block.return_file` (mkdir -p, 0600) taken from the brief before the sha check passes, so a tampered brief picks the write target. restoreRun writes to `binding.ledger` and `binding.record`, absolute paths from Drive that the sha256 binding does not cover. cmdLaunch prints `CHILD: pid=…` with exit 0 even when the spawn fails asynchronously (ENOENT is emitted after process.exit), and the parent then waits on a return file that never comes. The impact is low on a single-user machine, but the trust boundary is unvalidated.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: The Claude meter is fragile. A journal that is deleted, rotated or reset lowers the total, applyReading throws BUDGET_READING_REJECTED, and every later check exits 2 with no path forward except a meter change. nonceSessions() reads every top-level journal under <home>/.claude/projects fully into memory on each nonce bind, which is slow or out of memory on heavy users.

label: High
summary: **Resuming in a new Claude session silently keeps metering the old session.** `lib/ship-budget-cli.ts:254–264` only calls `bindClaude` and replaces the journal state when the meter *kind* changes. A normal `resume --record ... --session <new-session>` on an existing Claude run takes the same-meter branch, ignores the supplied session, and continues reading the old journals. Following the advertised recovery into a fresh session therefore makes new work invisible to the cap (and can retain the old context-threshold reading). Rebind a changed session with a new baseline while preserving previously charged usage.

label: High
summary: **Switching away from the estimate meter erases previously spent tokens.** `lib/ship-budget.ts:240–245` carries zero usage out of an estimate epoch, but `tally` only includes `estimate_used` while that meter is active. `resume --meter capy --reading ...` requires no cap-raise approval and makes those charges disappear. A read-only reproduction with the actual functions changed `used=20000000` to `used=0` after `newEpoch(..., METER_CONTRACTS.capy, ...)`. Carry and clear settled estimate usage when closing its epoch so switching meters cannot replenish the budget.

label: High
summary: **A partial or stopped child can mark the entire delegated segment complete.** `lib/ship-handoff.ts:156–170, 198–211` defaults `return` to `status=complete` without checking the child's stopped state or whether `--to` reaches its assigned endpoint. Reconciliation parses `to` but never checks it, and computes the next step from the *assigned* endpoint. For a Steps 7–11.5 handoff, `return --to 7` is accepted as complete and reconciliation advances to Step 12, skipping the reviews. The parser reproduction accepted `status=complete steps=7-7`. Require a valid terminal state and completed endpoint before advancing the parent.

label: High
summary: **Delegation drops the child's unmetered <reader> charges.** `lib/ship-handoff.ts:176–182, 200–205` retains only `used` from the child's BUDGET line and releases the entire child reservation without importing `unknown`. On Claude, `settleIn` deliberately records external <reader> dispatches as unknown because journals cannot see them. Those charges exist only in the child ledger; after reconciliation they vanish from the parent's admission total. Transfer those unknown charges exactly once, separately from journal usage, before releasing the reservation.

label: Medium
summary: **The parent's close audit rejects correctly reserved child reviews.** `lib/ship-budget.ts:345–359` scans every review row since the parent's creation, but matches only reservations in the parent's ledger. Delegated children share the review-log path and consume reservations in their own ledgers; `cmdReconcile` never imports their start tokens. A delegated review segment therefore produces BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED at parent close despite following the reservation protocol, unless an unrelated parent start happens to fall within the five-second matching window. Audit reservations across the reconciled child ledgers and bind rows by start identity rather than time proximity.

label: Medium
summary: **The estimate fallback cannot pass a fresh child's segment-entry check.** `lib/ship-budget-cli.ts:102–105` treats an unknown per-call charge as a delegation trigger even inside an already-fresh child. The estimate meter always returns an unknown call. Consequently a parent delegates at Step 7, but its fresh child stops immediately when admitting that same step; `--delegate never` also stops rather than providing a usable fallback. A read-only invocation of `decide` with a fresh estimate child, zero usage and a 1B cap returned exit 3 and `reason=context_threshold` entering Step 7. Distinguish admission into a newly delegated segment from a later context-growth boundary.

settleIn's unknown-charge branches have no test: `settle --unknown` (l.unknown += tokens) and the Claude-meter <reader> share (line 225) both change the next admission decision, yet no test settles with --unknown or settles a claude-meter batch containing <reader> and checks `unknown=` on the following BUDGET line.
fix: Add CLI tests: settle a dispatch reservation with --unknown and assert unknown=per_dispatch on the next check; on a --meter claude run, settle dispatch:specialist,<reader> and assert unknown=round(tokens/2).

summary: The `release` command has no test. Nothing checks that releasing an open reservation drops it from `reserved`, or that releasing a consumed or settled one leaves it alone.
fix: Add a test that reserves, releases, and asserts state=released plus reserved=0 on the next check; then release a consumed reservation and assert its state is unchanged.

summary: The timing guard asserts wall-clock bounds (full < 15s, incremental < max(250ms, full/4)) on a 30 MB journal. That is a timing-dependent assertion that can flake on a loaded CI runner.
fix: Assert that the read is incremental, for example that the stored file offset advances only by the appended bytes or that the second read parses one line, instead of timing it.

summary: The launch test polls for at most 5 s (50 x 100 ms) for the background fake child to write its args file, then reads the file unconditionally. On a slow runner it fails with ENOENT instead of a clear timeout.
fix: Use a longer deadline and assert the file exists before reading it, so a timeout shows up as a clear failure.

summary: The test claims every review-log --start in the dispatch sections takes a reservation, but it only checks that each file contains '--reservation' once. <reader>.md.tmpl has two `review-log --start` calls (review and review-fix-check), so either one could lose its reservation and the test would still pass.
fix: For each `gstack-review-log --start` occurrence, assert that '--reservation' appears in the same sentence or line. Repo-wide sweep: run /test-audit.

summary: Help text is cut from this file by hardcoded line numbers (slice(2, 26)), which overshoot the header comment by two lines. Running `gstack-ship-budget --help` prints a stray `/` and the source line `import { BudgetError } from '../lib/ship-budget';`. Any edit to the header will shift the window again.

summary: The context_threshold STOP line always prints threshold=DELEGATE_SEGMENT_CALL (150000). decide() also stops on the start threshold (DELEGATE_START_CALL, 100000) when a run starts with --delegate never, so in that case the message gives the wrong threshold.

summary: In unreservedDispatches, `reservedStarts.has(startFile.token)` is always true: startFile comes from the same reservations filtered on started_at and token, so the set check is dead code and `startFile` is misnamed. summary: nonceSessions synchronously reads every *.jsonl journal under <home>/.claude/projects in full (readFileSync to a string) just to find a nonce the agent echoed moments ago. A single journal larger than V8's string limit (~512MB) throws ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG, which is not a budgetError, so start fails instead of reporting BUDGET_METER_UNAVAILABLE.
fix: Scan only journals whose mtime falls within the last few minutes, since the nonce was just written, newest first. Read only each file's tail, or stream it in chunks, instead of readFileSync of the whole file.

test_stub: test('child x close',()=>{/* reserve child; close; expect row */})

summary: Every delegated capped run fails close: the child's dispatch reservations live in the child ledger, but it writes to the parent's review log, and unreservedDispatches checks parent reservations only. A properly reserved child review gets BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED, and close exits 3 with status=incomplete (reproduced).
fix: Include reconciled children's consumed reservations in the audit, or have each child audit its own rows.

summary: The branch marker outlives a stopped run, because budget_exhausted is a normal end and only close removes the marker. Afterwards a standalone /review, /codex review, or uncapped /ship on that branch is refused at review-log --start with BUDGET_CAP_REACHED or CHECK_SKIPPED (reproduced).
fix: Scope enforcement to the run, for example by passing the run id in the env, or remove or ignore the marker on stop and when an unmetered start runs.

summary: A Claude-meter resume in a fresh session (what the context_threshold RECOVER prescribes) keeps metering only the old session, because --session is ignored when the meter kind is unchanged. rebuildLedger binds no session at all. New spend is invisible and the cap is never enforced: 90M in session B left used at 1M (reproduced).
fix: Rebind or append --session on a same-meter resume and on rebuild; refuse when the bound journals are absent.

summary: Under meter=estimate, readMeter always returns call=null. Every Step 7 and Step 12 boundary therefore delegates, and with --delegate never it stops with context_threshold. The documented estimate setup for hosts without children can never pass Step 7 (reproduced).
fix: Do not treat an unknown call as over the threshold on meters that cannot measure calls.

summary: /ship Step 9 runs `review-log --start design-review-lite` with no reservation instruction, so under a cap admitReviewStart refuses it for frontend diffs.
fix: Tell the agent to reserve and pass --reservation there too, or exempt non-dispatch starts.

summary: newEpoch carries 0 when leaving meter=estimate, so estimate_used is dropped. Resuming an estimate run on Capy reset used from 4.5M to 0 (reproduced), which breaks the documented promise that a new epoch keeps prior usage.
fix: Carry estimate_used into carried_used when the closing epoch is estimate.

summary: [FIXABLE] [HIGH, gate bypass] A partial child return makes the parent skip the rest of the segment, including Step 11 adversarial review. lib/ship-handoff.ts:159 defaults `return --status` to `complete`. `--to` can be any step. cmdReconcile (lib/ship-handoff.ts:210) computes the parent's next step from the handoff's planned `h.to` and ignores the step the child reported (`ret.to`). So a child of segment 7–11.5 that runs `return --to 9` (forgetting --status, hitting its context, or misreading the brief) reconciles as `child=complete`, prints `next=12 verdict=continue` and exits 0. Steps 10–11.5 never run and nothing flags it. Fix: in reconcile, treat `ret.to !== h.to` as incomplete (exit 3), or derive `after` from `ret.to`. Make cmdReturn refuse `status=complete` when `--to` is not the segment's last step.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] [HIGH, silent enforcement bypass] Between a child's return and the parent's reconcile, dispatches are not checked against the budget at all. verify-handoff points the per-branch marker at the child ledger (lib/ship-handoff.ts:152). cmdReturn closes the child ledger (lib/ship-handoff.ts:170) but leaves the marker in place. activeLedger() treats a closed ledger as "no active run", so admitReviewStart() runs capture() with no reservation and no cap check. The marker only moves back when the parent reconciles. If the parent never reconciles (crash, missed step, or an agent that simply carries on), every later review dispatch skips the budget. Fix: on return (and on a child stop), point the marker back at `l.parent.ledger`. Have activeLedger fail closed when the marker names a closed child ledger.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] [HIGH, wrong-ledger routing] The child overwrites the parent's record block. The child ledger takes `record: block.record` (lib/ship-handoff.ts:141), and every child writeLedger rewrites the record's gstack-budget block with the child's run, ledger and role. Until the parent reconciles through `--run`, anything that resolves `--record` lands on the child ledger: `check --record`, `reconcile --record` (usage error: no handoff in the child run), `start --record` re-attach, `resume --record` after a crash, and `--rebuild-from-record`. The child's own stop prints `RECOVER: /ship --resume <record>`, which therefore resumes the child ledger with role=child and delegate=never. The parent's child reservation then stays open forever and the owner's cap raise goes to the wrong ledger. Fix: the child must not replace the parent's block. Write a separate child block, or keep the parent block authoritative and add a child pointer.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] [MEDIUM-HIGH, cap silently disabled] Rebuilding a Claude-metered ledger drops the session binding, so usage reads zero for the rest of the run. rebuildLedger builds `meter` without `sessions` or `config_dir` (lib/ship-budget-cli.ts:290). It also ignores `--session`. readMeter then calls newMeterState(..., []), readClaudeUsage finds no files, and every reading is 0, which passes the monotonic check. `used` freezes at `carried_used` and the cap stops working with no error. Rebuild also drops `parent` for a child ledger, so its stops never write the return file. Fix: write the bound sessions (and the parent link) into the record block. Refuse a claude rebuild unless the sessions can be restored or `--session` is passed.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] [MEDIUM, audit hole] The close-time audit of unreserved dispatches is effectively a time-window check. In unreservedDispatches (lib/ship-budget.ts:350-358), `reservedStarts` holds the tokens of every reservation that has `started_at`. `startFile` is chosen from exactly that set, so `reservedStarts.has(startFile.token)` is always true. Any review row whose start falls within 5 s of any consumed reservation counts as reserved, and one reservation can vouch for several rows. A dispatch started without `--reservation` alongside a reserved one in the same parallel batch (the documented pattern) passes the audit. Rows of other skills or concurrent runs on the same branch after `created_at` are attributed to this run. Fix: record the capture's `started_at` on the reservation and match one-to-one by exact value (or by the start token), consuming each reservation once.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: [INVESTIGATE] [MEDIUM, cross-run clobbering] The marker is keyed by sanitized branch name only (reviewPaths, lib/ship-budget.ts:288, at <state root>/projects/<slug>/<BRANCH>-ship-budget.json). bin/gstack-slug maps every detached HEAD to BRANCH=HEAD (verified: this checkout prints BRANCH=HEAD), and `a/b` and `a-b` collide. Two capped /ship runs in detached worktrees of the same repo, which is common for Capy and Captain lanes, share one marker. Run B's start retargets run A's review-log gate, so A's valid reservations are refused as "not in run". Run A's `close` (or a cap of none) unlinks the marker, which silently turns off B's enforcement. Needs a decision on the key: run id in the environment, worktree path, or HEAD plus worktree.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] [MEDIUM, wedge plus leaked reservations] Every ledger mutation mirrors to Drive inside the lock, and a mirror failure is fatal after the state is already written. writeLedger renames the ledger into place, rewrites the record, then calls mirrorRun (lib/ship-budget.ts:172) with no try/catch. On Capy that writes to <drive>/project-user-*/ship-budget on every check, settle and review-log start. A full drive, a write over the drive cap, or a slow FUSE write throws a non-BudgetError, which the bin rethrows as a crash. The ledger already holds the new reservation or consumed state, but no RESERVATION line or start token was printed. In admitReviewStart the start is captured and the reservation burned while review-log exits 1. Each such leak counts as reserved forever, so the run stops early. A Drive write slower than withFileLock's 60 s staleMs also lets a contender break the lock mid-write. Also, capyDriveFolder is called without `repo`, so on a machine with more than one project-user drive the checkpoint is silently skipped, even though the docs promise `resume --run` restores it. Fix: make the mirror best-effort (catch and warn) and run it outside the lock or after the critical write. Pass the repo to capyDriveFolder or report that no checkpoint was written.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] [MEDIUM, logic] A child delegated the whole run (Steps 1–22) is all but certain to stop at Step 7. decide() (lib/ship-budget-cli.ts:102-103) applies the segment boundary rule at `--next 7` and `--next 12` to children too, with `call === null || call >= 150k`. On Capy, call is null unless the agent passes `--prior-reading`, which is optional in the brief. On Claude Code, the per-call charge includes cache_read_input_tokens, which grows with context size, so by Step 7 it routinely exceeds 150k. A child never delegates, so it stops with context_threshold. Start-time delegation therefore produces an incomplete run instead of finishing. On Capy, the call delta (reading minus prior reading) also counts any parallel subagent spend in the thread, which inflates "call" and triggers spurious delegate or stop verdicts. Fix: hand out start delegation as 1–6.5 and let the parent delegate later segments, or skip the boundary rule for boundaries inside the child's own segment. Treat an unknown call as continue for children.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] [MEDIUM, budget double-spend] Nothing stops two children running the same handoff. verify-handoff only refuses a brief that is already reconciled. It mints a new child run, with the full sub_cap, every time it is called. cmdLaunch spawns a new detached `claude -p` on every call without marking the handoff as launched. A retried Capy subagent or a doubled `launch` gives two children that both write the record, commit and push, each admitting against a full sub-cap, while the parent reserved only one. Fix: record `verified_at` and the child run on the parent's handoff (under the parent lock), and refuse a second verify or launch.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: [INVESTIGATE] [MEDIUM, trust boundary] Unverified brief fields drive file writes. cmdVerifyHandoff writes `block.return_file` (lib/ship-handoff.ts:135) on the refusal path, which includes the case where the brief's sha256 matches no recorded handoff. So a foreign or edited brief chooses where a 0600 file is created or overwritten. cmdLaunch takes `block.parent_ledger` and `block.return_file` with no sha check (lib/ship-handoff.ts:232), mutates whatever ledger the brief names, opens a log next to an arbitrary path, and launches a headless child with `--permission-mode acceptEdits` and unrestricted Bash plus the full parent environment (API keys included). Exploiting this needs local write access to a brief the agent then runs, but the trust ordering is inverted. Fix: resolve the parent ledger first, find the handoff by sha, and use the recorded `h.return_file` and `h.file`. Never take write paths from an unverified block.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: [INVESTIGATE] [MEDIUM, governance] The "owner approval" for a cap raise is two free-text flags. `resume --token-cap <n> --approved-by <who> --words <text>` accepts any strings, and `resume --token-cap none` removes the cap and unlinks the marker. `close --approved-by --words` likewise waives every unreserved dispatch. The same agent that hit the cap can type "Garry" and continue. On Capy, `--reading` is also agent-supplied with no attestation, so under-reporting it defeats admission. The ledger journals the claim, but nothing ties it to a real owner message (for example a gstack-approvals record). Decide whether the budget is advisory (and document that) or requires verifiable approval.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] [LOW-MEDIUM, parsing] The record block cannot survive whitespace in paths. parseRecordBlock (lib/ship-budget.ts:264-270) splits `key=value` on \s+, and recordBlock writes `ledger=<absolute path>`. A state root with a space (Windows "C:<home>/First Last", or a custom GSTACK_STATE_ROOT) truncates `ledger`. Every `--record` call then fails with BUDGET_LEDGER_INVALID. cmdStart's re-attach misses and mints a fresh run, which loses the prior reservations and stop state. Fix: JSON-encode the block body.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: [INVESTIGATE] [LOW-MEDIUM, calibration makes the documented cap unusable] With the shipped constants (per_call 0.75M, per_dispatch 7.43M, stop_overhead 2.48M, default tail 2M), admitting Step 7 alone needs 12×0.75M + 7.43M + 4.48M = 20.9M of headroom. Under the docs' own example of `--token-cap 25M`, the run stops before Step 7 once used exceeds about 4.1M. The calibration notes cite real runs costing 39–49M. The example invites a cap that halts nearly every run as status=incomplete. The constants and the example need reconciling against completed ships.

summary: [FIXABLE] [LOW, resource] nonceSessions (lib/claude-usage.ts:54) does a synchronous full readFileSync of every top-level .jsonl in every <home>/.claude/projects directory to find a nonce. Long-lived Claude Code installs hold GBs of journals, which makes `start --nonce` slow and memory-heavy. Fix: filter by mtime (only sessions modified in the last hour) and stream-search.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: [INVESTIGATE] [LOW, wedge] If the Claude meter's file set shrinks mid-run (a subagent or child journal pruned or moved), readClaudeUsage resets and re-reads, and the total drops. readMeter saves the reset meter state before applyReading rejects the lower total, so every later check exits 2 with BUDGET_READING_REJECTED. Under the "any non-zero exit means the next step does not start" contract, the run is stuck until someone does a manual `resume --meter` epoch change. Consider carrying the last total forward instead of rejecting a meter-internal regression.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: [INVESTIGATE] [LOW] cmdStart re-attaches to any unclosed ledger named in the record's block (lib/ship-budget-cli.ts cmdStart), which contradicts the docs ("a /ship without --resume or --continue always starts a new run"). It silently ignores a new `--token-cap` and meter. An abandoned, unclosed earlier run on the same record path makes a fresh /ship inherit its cap and exit 3 if that run had stopped. Relatedly, bin/gstack-review-log swallows every settle failure on --finish (`|| true`), so failed settles leave reservations consumed, over-reserving until close. That fails safe but is silent apart from one stderr line.

label: High
summary: **High — A hash-invalid handoff can overwrite an arbitrary file.** `lib/ship-handoff.ts:120–135` reads `return_file` from the untrusted brief, detects that its SHA does not match any recorded handoff, and then writes the refusal to that same untrusted path. Changing only `return_file` in a legitimate brief to the invocation record or another writable file makes `verify-handoff` truncate that file while reporting `HANDOFF_PIN_MOVED`. The hash check therefore does not protect against tampering that causes data loss. Do not write anything using brief-supplied paths until authentication succeeds; refusal output must use a trusted destination from the parent ledger, or stdout only.

label: High
summary: **High — Resuming in a fresh Claude session silently stops metering the active session.** In `lib/ship-budget-cli.ts:254–264`, `--session` and `--nonce` are bound only when the meter kind changes. Resuming a Claude-metered run with `--meter claude --session <new-session>` takes the other branch and keeps the old session list and cached meter state. `readMeter` at lines 53–56 consequently keeps reading the old journal, even as the new session spends tokens. This is particularly relevant to the recovery instruction to resume a context-threshold stop in a fresh session: usage can remain frozen, reservations can repeatedly settle, and more work is admitted without charging the new session or asking for a cap increase. Rebind a changed Claude session even when the meter kind is unchanged, preserving prior usage and establishing the new session's baseline.

label: High
summary: **High — A partially completed child can advance the parent past mandatory ship steps.** `lib/ship-handoff.ts:156–171` accepts any valid `--to` step and defaults to `status=complete`; it does not require the assigned segment's endpoint or reject completion of a stopped child. Reconciliation parses the returned endpoint but never checks it, instead advancing after the originally assigned endpoint at lines 206–213. For a handoff of Steps 7–11.5, `return --to 7` produces a complete return that makes the parent continue at Step 12, skipping the remaining review segment. The parser also accepts a `RETURN` status of complete alongside a contradictory `GSTACK_RESULT` status. Require matching statuses and the assigned endpoint before accepting completion; incomplete coverage must not release the segment as successfully completed.

label: High
summary: **High — Reconciliation drops a Claude child's unmetered outside-review charges.** `settleIn` in `lib/ship-budget.ts:216–226` explicitly puts <reader> reservations into the child's `unknown` balance because Claude journals cannot see those tokens. However, `parseReturn` in `lib/ship-handoff.ts:175–182` extracts only `used`, and reconciliation at lines 200–205 releases the entire child reservation without adding its unknown charges to the parent. The parent's Claude journal reading cannot recover those charges. A child can therefore spend on an <reader>, return, and give that already-spent portion of its sub-cap back to the parent for another admission. Carry the child's unknown balance into the parent exactly once, including conservative accounting when no trustworthy final balance is available.

label: High
summary: **High — The same handoff can create multiple independently funded children.** `lib/ship-handoff.ts:123–153` checks only whether a handoff has been reconciled, then mints a fresh child ledger on every successful verification. It never atomically claims the handoff or records the admitted child's identity in the parent. Re-running verification before reconciliation, or starting two children concurrently, therefore gives each child the full sub-cap against the parent's single reservation. `launch` likewise permits repeated launches of the same brief. This admits multiple spenders and multiple writers of the shared checkout and invocation record without reserving their combined cost. Claim the handoff under the parent lock and make retries reattach to the same child, or refuse a second claimant.

label: Medium
summary: **Medium — Switching away from the estimate meter erases its settled spending.** `lib/ship-budget.ts:240–245` carries zero usage when the outgoing meter is `estimate`. Once the incoming meter is Capy or Claude, `tally` no longer includes `estimate_used`. A read-only, in-memory reproduction with 10,000,000 settled estimate tokens produced `used=10000000` before `newEpoch(..., METER_CONTRACTS.capy, ...)` and `used=0` afterward. `resume --meter capy --reading <n>` permits this transition without cap-raise approval, so recovery can silently replenish the budget. Transfer the outgoing estimate balance into carried usage and clear it in a way that also prevents double counting on subsequent switches.

label: Medium
summary: **Medium — The parent's final audit rejects correctly reserved child reviews.** `lib/ship-budget.ts:346–359` scans the shared branch review log from the parent's creation time but looks for reservations only in the parent's ledger. Delegated reviewers consume reservations in the child ledger, and reconciliation does not import their start evidence. Their valid review rows are consequently classified as unreserved by the parent, causing `close` to stop with `BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED` and demand an owner exception. Feeding a child review row to the audit with a settled parent child-reservation reproduces the false positive. Audit the reconciled descendants' reservation evidence, or give review rows an explicit run identity and account for delegation instead of treating every branch row as a direct parent dispatch.
